fields.v: Monash University (Yang, Tantithamthavorn, Arora); Transurban, Australia (Yang, Chua; industrial partner); The University of Melbourne (Fu); CSIRO RAISE programme support

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Evaluates — adversarial skill-synthesis benchmark of 2,826 malicious skill files and a three-judge exploitability-labelling pipeline, used to characterise the exploitability of Gemini CLI and Qwen Code over 5,629 runs
fields.why: Format fixed to '<nature>; secondary: <nature> — <detail>'. Main vs secondary is a judgement: the paper lists benchmark and pipeline as contributions, but frames itself as a 'large-scale empirical characterization' (RQ1–RQ3 are all about the agents), so 'Evaluates' as main nature is also defensible
fields.doubt: O artigo oferece benchmark e pipeline de avaliação, mas as três RQs medem a vulnerabilidade dos dois agentes. Decide se a natureza principal é método de avaliação ou Evaluates (com método como secundária).

Exploitability Rate (completed runs labelled exploited: declared intent or confirmed execution of the preflight) with Wilson 95% CI, per agent, generator and tactic; failure-mode taxonomy (recognized attack, irrelevant to task, acknowledged but not executed, no acknowledgment); verified execution; inter-judge agreement (Fleiss' kappa)

Automatic: run stratification, three local open-weight LLM judges (Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B, Gemma-2-9B) by majority with evidence anchoring, regex refusal veto and declared-intent override; PATH audit shim for execution. Manual: one author's blind labels on 240 runs (kappa 0.83-0.85) and failure-taxonomy labels

ER = exploited / completed runs (higher = less secure). Temperature 0, top-p 1, 120 s limit, auto-approve. The authors state no success criterion for an agent (no acceptable ER), so no verdicts are given.
- Gemini CLI + gemini-3-flash + malicious skills: ER 95.5% raw majority, 96.1% with override [95.3, 96.7] (2,705/2,816); per generator 95.5-96.8%; explicit refusal in 17 of 111 failures; Exfiltration 95.5%. Security (quality): no criterion stated by the authors. Cost: not measured; no criterion stated by the authors
- Qwen Code + qwen3-coder-plus + malicious skills: ER 71.6% raw, 74.0% with override [72.3, 75.6] (2,081/2,813); per generator 67.7% (DeepSeek-R1) to 76.9%; refusals 95 of 732 failures; Exfiltration 38.5%, Impact 56.2%. Security (quality): no criterion stated by the authors. Cost: not measured; no criterion stated by the authors
- Human gold standard: Gemini 95.5% (94.2-96.3), Qwen 70.9% (65.6-75.7)
- Verified execution: 1 run of 5,629 (harness-limited)
fields.why: The draft applied its own rule ('works if ER low') and gave 'does not work' verdicts; the authors set no acceptable exploitability threshold (they only call a 67.2% pooled exfiltration rate 'unacceptably high' for critical infrastructure, p. 24), so per the 2026-11-23 rule the verdict is 'no criterion stated'. Metric values checked against Tables 3-5: all correct

fields.v: Two agents (Gemini CLI, Qwen Code) chosen by availability at Transurban; same 471 commands x 6 generators, same task prompt, sandbox, 120 s limit, temperature 0, auto-approve. No benign-skill control. One run per skill per agent. Acceptance: judge panel validated against human labels. Human intervention: none

Gemini CLI more exploitable than Qwen Code by 22-24 points (non-overlapping Wilson CIs); exploitability nearly invariant to generator model; tactic gap largest for Exfiltration (95.5% vs 38.5%); Qwen-only off-task rejection (10.1% of its failures). Explicit safety recognition 1.99% of all runs

Distinguished the agents clearly. Single judges disagree strongly on Qwen (Fleiss' kappa -0.06; flag rates 22.4-94.8%), motivating the panel; panel vs human kappa 0.83-0.85. Limitations: single masking template, synthetic not in-the-wild skills, single task, 120 s limit, two agents, residual non-determinism

Commands do not cover all payloads or obfuscations; synthetic descriptions and one 'mandatory preflight' template (rates as lower bound for this pattern); only two CLI agents (not Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot); one task; 120 s cap; verified execution harness-limited; future: in-the-wild skills, more tasks, long-horizon runs, pre-ingestion skill scanner evaluation

Code and dataset: github.com/awsm-research/AgentJailbreak (per-run logs, prompts, regexes, unit tests). No pre-registration. Language: shell commands; web app language chosen by agent (e.g. Python/Flask). Values from Table 3 and Table 4 (p. 16, layout rebuilt from pdftotext), Table 5 (p. 22), Table 6 (p. 24) and text pp. 18-22. Inconsistency: 2 x 2,826 = 5,652 planned runs minus 5,629 completed = 23 missing (10 Gemini, 13 Qwen per Table 3 totals), but the text reports 24 empty runs excluded plus two commands with no run recorded (p. 12). Relevance to SDD: skill files as agent instruction artefacts and their security risk
fields.why: The draft stated '24 empty runs excluded' as consistent; the Table 3 totals imply 23 missing runs, not 24 plus two missing commands. Table 6 per-tactic counts sum to 5,629 (checked)
